plugins.name: Cargo bike
plugins.description: How far an electric cargo tricycle gets out and back on one battery charge, over the hills and preferring bike lanes, and what it saves against a car (purchase, fuel, tax, insurance, parking, maintenance), in its own tab.

calculations.label: Cargo bike range
calculations.description: Round trip from a start point to a destination on bike-usable streets (preferring bike lanes) with the battery used over the terrain, and a range map of how far the bike gets out and back in every direction.

calculations.label: Cargo bike savings
calculations.description: Yearly cost of the cargo bike against a car for the same trips: purchase, energy, tax, insurance, parking and maintenance, in the currency of the start point's country.

style._comment: The range map (area reachable out and back on one charge), the trip there and back coloured by the kind of street, the bike-lane gap picked in the tab, and the charging points and bike parkings along the route. Class ids come from crates/cargo-bike (Class), amenity kinds from the API's bike-amenity tiles.

plugins.name: Energy and emissions
plugins.description: Traction energy and greenhouse gas emissions of every line a year, per mode and for the network, from the vehicle-km each line runs: electricity at the substation or charger, diesel in litres, and CO2e from the grid's emission intensity and diesel well-to-wheel. Shown in the Tables tab.

calculations.label: Energy and emissions
calculations.description: Electricity, diesel, final energy and CO2e a year per line, per mode and for the network, with the intensity per vehicle-km and per place-km.

energy.electric_share.label: Share of vehicle-km run on electricity

energy.charging_loss_share.label: Charging loss, share of the energy taken from the battery

plugins.name: Esri World Imagery
plugins.description: Esri World Imagery as an aerial basemap: aerial photos at about 0.3 to 1 m per pixel in most cities, sharp enough to see lanes, kerbs and track. Offered once an Admin saves an ArcGIS API key and accepts Esri's terms under Administration → Plugins; the tiles come through this MobSimLab, so browsers never see the key, and are not stored.

basemaps.label: Esri World Imagery
basemaps.note: Aerial photos at about 0.3 to 1 m per pixel in most cities, coarser in the countryside: sharp enough to see lanes, kerbs and track. Photo dates vary by place.

attribution.text: Powered by Esri · Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics, and the GIS User Community

plugins.name: Ferries
plugins.description: Passenger ferries and water buses drawn with the water route kit: piers with berths and gangways, routes over water, speed zones and a berth check (ADR-0037). Car ferries come later.

tools.label: Ferry
tools.hint: Water buses and crossings: click piers, shape the route over water.

ferry.harbour_speed_kn.label: Speed limit in a new speed zone

ferry.layover_s.label: Layover at the ends of a line, minimum

ferry.pax_per_call_share.label: Passengers on and off at the busiest call, share of capacity

ferry.reserve_share.label: Reserve vessels, share of the vessels in service

ferry.cost.vessel_hour.label: Ferry crew, fuel and running repairs per vessel-hour

plugins.name: GTFS import and export
plugins.description: Reads a GTFS feed (zip) into the project as an existing network for one service day, cut to the map view if asked, so the journey planner rides it with the planned lines; and writes the project's lines as a GTFS feed for other tools.

importers.label: GTFS feed
importers.description: Stops, routes and the trips of one service day (the busiest Wednesday unless a date is given), with frequencies.txt as frequency patterns and route types as modes.

exporters.label: GTFS feed
exporters.description: The project's lines as a weekday GTFS feed: exact trips, frequency lines as frequencies.txt, stations for stop groups.

plugins.name: NASA GIBS imagery
plugins.description: Satellite imagery from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) as aerial basemaps, for a day you pick: Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 at about 30 m per pixel and VIIRS at about 250 m. No API key is needed. The imagery is too coarse to see streets or track.

basemaps.label: NASA HLS Sentinel-2
basemaps.note: About 30 m per pixel (38 m on this map), from one day's satellite passes: parts of the map are empty or cloudy, so try another date. Too coarse to draw track or kerbs.

attribution.text: NASA GIBS: HLS Sentinel-2 (HLSS30 v2.0), contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data

basemaps.label: NASA HLS Landsat 8 and 9
basemaps.note: About 30 m per pixel (38 m on this map), from one day's satellite passes: parts of the map are empty or cloudy, so try another date. Too coarse to draw track or kerbs.

attribution.text: NASA GIBS: HLS Landsat 8 and 9 (HLSL30 v2.0), courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey

basemaps.label: NASA VIIRS true colour
basemaps.note: The whole world each day at about 250 m per pixel (306 m on this map), with clouds: for regional context only.

attribution.text: NASA GIBS: VIIRS NOAA-20 Corrected Reflectance

plugins.name: Noise map
plugins.description: Estimated noise of the service lines (ADR-0038): a live noise band while drawing street lines and railways, with checks for curve squeal, bridges and switches. CNOSSOS-EU road and railway emission, free field without buildings for now.

calculations.label: Noise band
calculations.description: L_den and L_night of the drawn lines at 4 m, free field: band distances either side, a receiver grid for the map and checks.

style._comment: The noise band is drawn as a picture of the receiver grid (raster), coloured in 5 dB bands after ISO 1996-2 / DIN 45682. Colours are applied by the engine (noise::band_colour); this layer sets how the picture is shown. The difference map between two scenarios (step N3) is coloured by the change in dB: `difference` gives each class's lower edge (null: no lower edge) and colour (null: not drawn).

noise.band_lnight_db.label: Noise corridor edge in the editors, L_night

noise.ground_factor_default.label: Ground factor G where land use is unknown (0 hard, 1 soft)

plugins.name: WMS, WMTS and XYZ map layers
plugins.description: Map layers from WMS, WMTS and XYZ tile services, as basemaps or overlays. An Admin adds a service under Administration → Plugins, with its sign-in details if needed; tiles come through this MobSimLab, so browsers never see them.

plugins.name: On-demand bus
plugins.description: Demand-responsive transport drawn with the service zone kit: outline a zone, set the requests an hour, the fleet and the service hours, and get the vehicles needed, the average wait, ride and door-to-door time from continuous-approximation formulas. Simulate the day dispatches every booking trip by trip (ADR-0042). The zone shows in the journey planner.

tools.label: On-demand bus
tools.hint: Minibuses booked by app: outline the zone, set the fleet and hours.

drt.target_utilisation.label: Busy share of the fleet that keeps waits short

drt.pooling_detour_share.label: Extra ride time from sharing, over the direct trip

drt.max_wait_limit_s.label: Longest wait before a booking is turned away

drt.max_detour_share.label: Longest ride, share over the direct ride

drt.max_detour_fixed_s.label: Longest ride, fixed allowance over the direct ride

plugins.name: Panoramax street photos
plugins.description: Street-level photos from Panoramax, the free and open street photo commons. Open Street photos on the map to see where photos were taken, then click a point to see the photos taken near it. The photos are under open licences that allow mapping from them. No key is needed. Photos come through this MobSimLab and are not stored or saved with the project.

streetPhotos.label: Panoramax
streetPhotos.note: Photos shared by people and public bodies, under open licences (mostly CC BY-SA 4.0 or Etalab 2.0) that allow mapping from them. Credit the author when you use one.

plugins.name: People movers
plugins.description: Cable-hauled automated people movers on an elevated guideway, drawn with the straight spans kit: shuttles with two trains, and pinched loops with detachable trains that stop in every station (ADR-0037 §7). Self-propelled people movers need the railway editor and come later.

options.label: Shuttle, two trains on a fixed rope

tools.label: People mover
